scope: Native Apple M5 Pro Metal equipment and pause inspection

observations.result: One assertion failed: paused render counter advanced once from 435 to 436 after a 250 ms settling delay and during a 350 ms observation window. Native active p95 was 9.30 ms. The failed full report was superseded by the rerun; this note preserves the observation.
Sixteen samples over approximately 1.6 seconds all reported frame counter 254 and sampleCount 0. Continuous rendering was not reproduced.

Passed. Paused counter 457 to 457; offscreen counter 478 to 478; fan and LED animation freezes passed for Pause, equipment disabled, and reduced motion. Actual fan phases and LED colors changed while active.

interpretation: The first attempt observed a single late demand frame. Its cause was not established. A layout or other one-off invalidation is plausible, but not proven. No renderer change was made to conceal the observation. The targeted trace and unchanged complete rerun passed.
visualReview: Before/after canvas captures show different fan-blade orientations and visible small amber rack LEDs. LED changes are deliberately subtle. Model surfaces remain readable on the black background.

retentionObservation.graphics: Every observed session reported the same geometry, texture, and estimated asset allocation counts. This does not measure total driver memory.
retentionObservation.interpretation: The 8 MiB smoke-test ceiling passed, with nonzero observed JS heap growth. This is bounded short-run evidence, not proof of zero retention or a long-duration leak test. Framework/router/compiler caches and cleanup timing can contribute; no heap-retaining path was proven.
retentionObservation.staticReview: Session cleanup aborts work and disposes its owned model; asset ownership releases geometries, materials, textures, ImageBitmaps and InstancedMesh resources once. Event listeners and the opt-in snapshot closure are removed. R3F 9.8 tears down after its reconciler cleanup commits and loses the old GL context. No application-global mutable scene cache or explicit per-session retention collection was found. Resource-owner identity Sets intentionally survive until late parsing callbacks settle and then become collectible with their session.
